about: Touched-path → test-suite map, read by the landing gate, which derives every landing's touched paths from its diff and requires the commands mapped here green. First matching rule wins: specific rules above broad ones. `tests: []` means CONSCIOUSLY untested and must carry its why. An unmapped path fails the resolver loud. Commands run from the repo root.

rules.why: the guard test pins the landing-matrix commands so a config cannot be silently dropped from the rule below
prose, licenses, and evidence artifacts (screenshots/logs recorded under docs/evidence)

tests: nix-shell -p shellcheck python3 --run 'shellcheck scripts/sally/export.sh && python3 -m py_compile scripts/sally/*.py'
rules.why: the purchased-mesh export; running it needs the private .blend, so offline it gets lint and syntax checks only
operator tooling (terrain bake, asset fetch) — exercised by use, no offline harness

the browser build/serve/verify harness (rl#411 stages 5-6) — a live harness exercised by RUNNING run.sh (verify drives headless chromium; no offline harness); shellcheck + node syntax checks keep it mechanically sound, and game-web/src/ rides the general rust rule below
the pinned dev environment — every mapped suite below runs inside it, so a break fails those commands loudly

tests: nix-shell --run 'cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p net-proto -p net-link -p game-web'
rules.why: AGENTS.md's pre-submission contract, workspace-wide, plus the rl#411 platform-freedom check: net-proto (the protocol core), net-link (the link layer — its web half only compiles on wasm32) and game-web (the browser entry — checking it compiles the ENTIRE web leaf: net+crab-world with render on wasm32) must stay wasm32-green, and the wasm build breaks from DEP-side edits too, so the check rides every rust touch; it is a seconds-cheap cargo check when warm. The crates interlock (net/game consume crab-world's sim seams), so per-crate scoping would miss cross-crate breakage; assets ride the same rule because the suite consumes them (the terrain bake, controls glyphs). The isolated `--release -p game` build is the shipped binary's own feature set, which workspace feature-unification would mask
